name: isUndefined
summary: Checks whether a value is exactly `undefined`.
summaryReturn: `true` if the value is `undefined`; otherwise `false`.
description: Use this check to distinguish `undefined` from `null` and other empty-looking values. It does not convert the input.

name: isNull
summary: Checks whether a value is exactly `null`.
summaryReturn: `true` if the value is `null`; otherwise `false`.
description: Use this check when `null` has a different meaning from `undefined`. To accept both, use `isNullish`.

name: isBoolean
summary: Checks whether a value is a primitive boolean or a boxed `Boolean`.
notes:
Uses the built-in wrapper operation to read the stored value. Overridden `valueOf` methods and `Symbol.toStringTag` properties are ignored; prototype imitations and proxies around wrappers return `false`.

The TypeScript result is `boolean`: a structural wrapper interface does not prove native identity. For primitive-only narrowing, use native `typeof` checks.
summaryReturn: `true` if the value is a primitive boolean or boxed `Boolean`; otherwise `false`.
description: Accepts both primitive boolean values and wrapper objects such as `new Boolean(false)`, including wrappers from another realm. It checks the stored native value without converting other inputs.
tooltip: Accepts wrappers from another realm, but rejects prototype imitations and proxies around wrappers. Does not invoke overridden conversion methods.

name: isNumber
summary: Checks whether a value is a primitive number or a boxed `Number`.
notes:
Uses the built-in wrapper operation to read the stored value. Overridden `valueOf` methods and `Symbol.toStringTag` properties are ignored; prototype imitations and proxies around wrappers return `false`.

The TypeScript result is `boolean`: a structural wrapper interface does not prove native identity. For primitive-only narrowing, use native `typeof` checks.
summaryReturn: `true` if the value is a primitive number or boxed `Number`, including `NaN` and infinities; otherwise `false`.
description: Accepts both primitive number values and wrapper objects such as `new Number(42)`, including wrappers from another realm. It checks the stored native value without converting other inputs. `NaN` and positive or negative infinity are numbers for this check.
tooltip: Accepts wrappers from another realm, but rejects prototype imitations and proxies around wrappers. Does not invoke overridden conversion methods. Includes `NaN` and infinities.

name: isString
summary: Checks whether a value is a primitive string or a boxed `String`.
notes:
Uses the built-in wrapper operation to read the stored value. Overridden `valueOf` methods and `Symbol.toStringTag` properties are ignored; prototype imitations and proxies around wrappers return `false`.

The TypeScript result is `boolean`: a structural wrapper interface does not prove native identity. For primitive-only narrowing, use native `typeof` checks.
summaryReturn: `true` if the value is a primitive string or boxed `String`; otherwise `false`.
description: Accepts both primitive string values and wrapper objects such as `new String('hello')`, including wrappers from another realm. It checks the stored native value without converting other inputs.
tooltip: Accepts wrappers from another realm, but rejects prototype imitations and proxies around wrappers. Does not invoke overridden conversion methods.

name: isSymbol
summary: Checks whether a value is a primitive symbol.
notes: Unlike `isBoolean`, `isNumber` and `isString`, this check does not accept a wrapper object. Use `toSymbol` to unbox a Symbol wrapper when conversion is intended.
summaryReturn: `true` if the value is a primitive symbol; otherwise `false`.
description: Accepts symbols such as `Symbol("key")`. A boxed symbol, created with `Object(symbol)`, returns `false`.
tooltip: Boxed symbols return `false`.

name: isBigInt
summary: Checks whether a value is a primitive bigint.
notes: Unlike `isBoolean`, `isNumber` and `isString`, this check does not accept a wrapper object. Strings and numbers are not converted; use `toBigInt` when conversion is intended.
summaryReturn: `true` if the value is a primitive bigint; otherwise `false`.
description: Accepts primitive bigint values without converting strings or numbers. A boxed bigint returns `false`.
tooltip: Boxed bigints return `false`; numeric strings are not converted.

name: isPrimitive
summary: Checks whether a value is a primitive rather than an object or function.
notes: The browser object `document.all` returns `false`, even though its historical `typeof` result is `"undefined"`. The check uses the same object/function boundary as `isObject`.
summaryReturn: `true` if the value is a primitive, including `null` or `undefined`; otherwise `false`.
description: Accepts `null`, `undefined`, booleans, numbers, strings, bigints and symbols. Wrapper objects and functions return `false`. This is the complement of `isObject`, including for the browser object `document.all`.
tooltip: Includes `null` and `undefined`; rejects wrappers and functions.

name: isNullish
summary: Checks whether a value is `null` or `undefined`.
notes: Uses strict comparisons with `null` and `undefined`. The browser object `document.all` returns `false`, despite its historical loose equality with `null`.
summaryReturn: `true` if the value is `null` or `undefined`; otherwise `false`.
description: Use this check for absent values while retaining `0`, `false` and the empty string. Unlike loose comparison with `null`, it does not treat the browser object `document.all` as absent.

name: isEmpty
summary: Checks whether a value is nullish, an empty string, or an empty supported collection.
notes:
Strings, Maps and Sets, and validated array-like lengths are checked first. For other inputs, callable iterator methods or `next` take precedence over dictionary keys and cause `TypeError`. These methods are detected but never called. This also applies to plain dictionaries exposing those capabilities.

Remaining plain dictionaries are empty when they have no own enumerable string keys. Unsupported values, such as numbers or Dates, return `false`. Property getters and proxy traps can still run: avoiding iteration does not guarantee a check without side effects.

Handle iteration explicitly when consumption is intended. Unavailable native collection types do not prevent loading or checks of other supported values. If a detected collection lacks the required native size or iteration operation, the check throws `TypeError`.
summaryReturn: `true` if the value is nullish, an empty string, or an empty supported collection; otherwise `false`.
description: Checks strings and [supported collections](#empty-and-blank-values) without consuming an iterator. `null` and `undefined` count as empty; `[null]` does not. Unsized iterators and iterables throw because their contents cannot be checked without consumption. Check the expected type first when requiring a non-empty string or collection. Item validity is a separate check.
tooltip: Check the expected type before using negation to require contents. Uses lengths, collection sizes or dictionary keys. Unsized iterators and iterables throw `TypeError`; getters and proxy traps may run. Unavailable native collection types do not prevent loading or checks of other supported values. If a detected collection lacks the required native size or iteration operation, the check throws `TypeError`.
errors: `TypeError` for unsized iterators or iterables. Property getters and proxy traps may throw. See [Empty and blank values](#empty-and-blank-values).

name: isBlank
summary: Checks whether a value is nullish, an empty or whitespace-only string, or a supported collection containing only nullish values.
notes:
Uses the same input order and unsized-input errors as `isEmpty`. Map checks examine values, Set checks examine items, and dictionary checks examine own enumerable string-keyed values. Iterator capabilities take precedence over plain-dictionary handling.

The check is shallow: every inspected value must be `null` or `undefined`. Empty strings and empty objects inside a collection are not nullish. Unavailable native collection types do not prevent loading or checks of other supported values. If a detected collection lacks the required native size or iteration operation, the check throws `TypeError`.
summaryReturn: `true` if the value is nullish, an empty or whitespace-only string, or a supported collection containing only nullish values; otherwise `false`.
description: Accepts nullish values, empty or whitespace-only strings, and [supported collections](#empty-and-blank-values) whose contents are all `null` or `undefined`. The check is shallow: `[null]` is blank, but `[""]` is not. Unsized iterators and iterables throw instead of being consumed. Check for a string before using negation to require text.
tooltip: Check for a string before using negation to require text. Shallow and non-consuming. Map checks inspect values. Unsized iterators and iterables throw `TypeError`; getters and proxy traps may run. Unavailable native collection types do not prevent loading or checks of other supported values. If a detected collection lacks the required native size or iteration operation, the check throws `TypeError`.
errors: `TypeError` for unsized iterators or iterables. Property getters and proxy traps may throw. See [Empty and blank values](#empty-and-blank-values).

name: isTruthy
summary: Checks whether JavaScript treats a value as `true` in a condition.
summaryReturn: `true` if the value is truthy under JavaScript boolean coercion; otherwise `false`.
description: Uses ordinary boolean coercion: non-empty strings and objects are truthy, including `"false"`, `[]` and `new Boolean(false)`. It does not parse boolean text.

name: isFalsy
summary: Checks whether JavaScript treats a value as `false` in a condition.
summaryReturn: `true` if the value is falsy under JavaScript boolean coercion; otherwise `false`.
description: Returns the opposite of `isTruthy`. This includes values such as `false`, `0`, `""`, `null`, `undefined` and `NaN`; it does not mean only absent values.

name: isInteger
summary: Checks whether a primitive or boxed number is an integer.
notes:
Reads Number wrappers with the built-in unboxing operation, ignoring overridden conversion methods. Other coercible values are rejected.

The TypeScript result is `boolean`. A failed numeric refinement must not imply that the input is no longer a number.
summaryReturn: `true` if the value is a primitive or boxed finite integral number; otherwise `false`.
description: Finite whole numbers pass; fractional values, `NaN` and infinities do not. `Number` wrappers are inspected without calling overridden conversion methods. Numeric strings and other coercible values return `false`.
tooltip: Accepts `Number` wrappers without invoking conversion hooks; rejects numeric strings.

name: isSafeInteger
summary: Checks whether a primitive or boxed number is an integer in JavaScript’s safe-integer range.
notes:
Reads Number wrappers with the built-in unboxing operation, ignoring overridden conversion methods. Other coercible values are rejected.

The TypeScript result is `boolean`. A failed numeric refinement must not imply that the input is no longer a number.
summaryReturn: `true` if the value is a primitive or boxed integer within the safe-integer range; otherwise `false`.
description: Accepts integers from `-9007199254740991` through `9007199254740991`, inclusive. `Number` wrappers are inspected without calling overridden conversion methods. Numeric strings and other coercible values return `false`.
tooltip: Accepts `Number` wrappers without invoking conversion hooks; rejects numeric strings.

name: isFloat
summary: Checks whether a primitive or boxed number is a finite number with a fractional part.
notes:
Reads Number wrappers with the built-in unboxing operation, ignoring overridden conversion methods. Other coercible values are rejected.

The TypeScript result is `boolean`. A failed numeric refinement must not imply that the input is no longer a number.
summaryReturn: `true` if the value is a primitive or boxed finite non-integer number; otherwise `false`.
description: A number such as `1.5` passes; whole numbers, `NaN` and infinities do not. `Number` wrappers are inspected without calling overridden conversion methods. Numeric strings and other coercible values return `false`.
tooltip: Accepts `Number` wrappers without invoking conversion hooks; rejects numeric strings.

name: isFinite
summary: Checks whether a primitive or boxed number is a finite number.
notes:
Reads Number wrappers with the built-in unboxing operation, ignoring overridden conversion methods. Other coercible values are rejected.

The TypeScript result is `boolean`. A failed numeric refinement must not imply that the input is no longer a number.
summaryReturn: `true` if the value is a primitive or boxed finite number; otherwise `false`.
description: Rejects `NaN` and positive or negative infinity. `Number` wrappers are inspected without calling overridden conversion methods. Numeric strings and other coercible values return `false`.
tooltip: Accepts `Number` wrappers without invoking conversion hooks; rejects numeric strings.

name: isInfinite
summary: Checks whether a primitive or boxed number is positive or negative infinity.
notes:
Reads Number wrappers with the built-in unboxing operation, ignoring overridden conversion methods. Other coercible values are rejected.

The TypeScript result is `boolean`. A failed numeric refinement must not imply that the input is no longer a number.
summaryReturn: `true` if the value is primitive or boxed positive or negative infinity; otherwise `false`.
description: Accepts `Infinity` and `-Infinity`; finite numbers and `NaN` do not pass. `Number` wrappers are inspected without calling overridden conversion methods. Numeric strings and other coercible values return `false`.
tooltip: Accepts `Number` wrappers without invoking conversion hooks; rejects numeric strings.

name: isNaN
summary: Checks whether a primitive or boxed number is `NaN`.
notes:
Reads Number wrappers with the built-in unboxing operation, ignoring overridden conversion methods. Other coercible values are rejected.

The TypeScript result is `boolean`. A failed numeric refinement must not imply that the input is no longer a number.
summaryReturn: `true` if the value is primitive or boxed `NaN`; otherwise `false`.
description: Detects the not-a-number value without converting strings or other inputs. `Number` wrappers are inspected without calling overridden conversion methods. Numeric strings and other coercible values return `false`.
tooltip: Accepts `Number` wrappers without invoking conversion hooks; rejects numeric strings.

name: isNumeric
summary: Checks whether a value is a finite number, a bigint, or non-blank numeric text.
notes: Uses standard numeric conversion syntax, not a decimal-only grammar. It rejects `NaN`, `Infinity`, empty/whitespace-only strings, boolean values, boxed `BigInt` values and arbitrary coercible objects. A passing string need not be exactly representable or within the safe-integer range; underflow to zero still passes.
summaryReturn: `true` if the value is a finite primitive or boxed number, a primitive bigint, or non-blank string text converting to a finite number; otherwise `false`.
description: Use this check when numeric strings should be accepted without converting the caller’s value. Primitive and boxed finite numbers, primitive bigints, and primitive or boxed strings that convert to finite numbers pass. Empty or whitespace-only strings do not.
tooltip: Accepts numeric text as well as finite numbers and primitive bigints. Rejects booleans, blank text, `NaN`, infinities and boxed bigints.

name: isObject
summary: Checks whether a value is a non-null object or function.
notes: Uses the JavaScript object/function boundary, so objects from another realm pass without needing a local `instanceof Object` match. The browser object `document.all` also passes despite its legacy `typeof` result.
summaryReturn: `true` if the value is a non-null object or function; otherwise `false`.
description: Accepts objects of any supported shape, including arrays, dates, wrapper objects and functions. It does not require a plain dictionary or a particular prototype. `null` returns `false`.

name: isPlainObject
summary: Checks whether a value has a null or ordinary `Object` prototype.
notes: An own `constructor` field is ordinary data and is not read. Assigning `null` or `Object.prototype` as another object’s prototype can change the result. The browser object `document.all` follows this current-prototype rule too; its usual `HTMLAllCollection` prototype does not pass. This is a prototype classification, not a record of how the value was allocated or a validation of its fields.
summaryReturn: `true` if the value has a null or ordinary `Object` prototype; otherwise `false`.
description: Recognises ordinary object literals and null-prototype dictionaries, including from another realm. Arrays and class instances with their usual prototypes do not pass. This classifies the current prototype; it does not prove how the value was created or validate its fields.
tooltip: Checks the current prototype, not allocation history or a schema. Proxy traps may run; an own `constructor` field is not read.
errors: Property getters or proxy traps may throw; their errors propagate.

name: isCircular
summary: Checks whether a value contains a circular reference through enumerable string-keyed properties, Map keys and values, or Set members.
notes:
A cycle must lead back to an object on the current path. Shared acyclic objects are allowed; a `false` result does not establish that objects are independently copied or detached from another model. Symbols, non-enumerable properties, WeakMap/WeakSet entries and arbitrary iterable contents are excluded.

Property keys are captured when an object is first visited; their values are read as traversal proceeds. Map keys precede their corresponding values. Stored collection references are collected through captured native `forEach` operations after ordinary properties. Application iterators and method overrides do not select collection contents; their eligible ordinary properties are still inspected.

Keep the graph stable during inspection, including from getters. The result concerns references observed during the call, not an immutable snapshot. Iterative traversal avoids recursive stack growth, and completed shared objects are inspected once. Internal reference tracking falls back to local arrays when weak collections are unavailable; no platform globals are changed.

Native collection recognition uses available captured local operations and supports instances from other realms. If native detection is unavailable, only ordinary properties are inspected. A recognised Map or Set without native `forEach` support throws `TypeError` when its contents are reached. Missing optional capabilities do not prevent package loading or checks of unrelated objects. This check does not establish JSON serialisability or safety for an operation that follows different references.
summaryReturn: `true` if following the supported references leads back to an object already on the current path; otherwise `false`.
description: Includes inherited enumerable properties and follows Map keys, Map values and Set members. Shared references without a cycle are allowed. Ordinary properties are inspected before collection contents.
tooltip: Includes inherited enumerable string properties and Map and Set contents. Symbols, non-enumerable properties and WeakMap/WeakSet entries are excluded. Getters and proxy traps may run and throw; keep the graph stable. Missing native detection limits inspection to ordinary properties; a recognised collection without native traversal support throws `TypeError`.
errors: Property getters and proxy traps may throw; their errors propagate. Requested Map/Set content inspection throws `TypeError` when native traversal support is unavailable.

name: isIterable
summary: Checks whether a value exposes a synchronous iterator method.
notes: The `Symbol.iterator` property is read, but its method is not called. A getter or proxy trap can run or throw, and a callable method can still return an invalid iterator.
summaryReturn: `true` if the value has a callable `Symbol.iterator` method; otherwise `false`.
description: Returns `true` when `Symbol.iterator` is callable. The method is not invoked, so this detects the capability without consuming the value or proving that iteration will work.
tooltip: Reads `Symbol.iterator` without calling it. Getters and proxy traps may run; method presence does not guarantee a valid iterator.
errors: Property getters or proxy traps may throw; their errors propagate.

name: isArray
summary: Checks whether a value is an array, including from another realm.
notes: Uses the `Array.isArray` function captured when the module loads. This retains native behaviour for arrays from another realm and proxies, including `TypeError` for a revoked proxy.
summaryReturn: `true` if the value passes native `Array.isArray`; otherwise `false`.
description: Uses native `Array.isArray` behaviour. Arrays and non-revoked proxies around arrays pass; array-like objects do not. A revoked proxy throws.
tooltip: Preserves native `Array.isArray` behaviour, including `TypeError` for a revoked proxy.
errors: `TypeError` for a revoked proxy, following native `Array.isArray` behaviour.

name: ensureArray
summary: Returns an existing array unchanged or wraps a supplied value as one item. Without arguments, returns an empty array.
notes:
Arrays retain their identity, including empty, sparse, frozen, subclassed and foreign arrays. Other supplied values, including `null` and `undefined`, are single items; strings and other collections are not expanded. A preserved array is not an independent copy. Omitting the argument creates a fresh empty array. Additional callback arguments are ignored.

TypeScript infers item, array and tuple types while preserving readonly restrictions. It does not promise custom array-subtype properties. Inputs typed only as `object`, `unknown` or `{}` have conservative `readonly unknown[]` results because they may hide arrays. Inference follows declared array structure; TypeScript cannot prove native array identity for fabricated array-shaped objects. Pass such inputs as `unknown` when their native identity is uncertain. Direct `map(ensureArray)` calls work but infer broad results; use `map(value => ensureArray(value))` for precise element inference. A zero-argument call can select the element type, for example `ensureArray<number>()`.
summaryReturn: A new empty array when no value is supplied; otherwise the original array or a new array containing the supplied value.
description: Use this for inputs that accept one item or an array. Omission differs from an explicitly supplied undefined value. Use [toArray](#toarrayvalue) to extract supported input contents into a new shallow array.
tooltip: Without arguments, creates a fresh empty array; explicit `null` and `undefined` remain items. Preserves array identity and sparse slots without iteration or coercion. TypeScript retains element and readonly tuple types; broad `object` and `unknown` inputs remain conservative. A preserved array is not a copy.
errors: Native `Array.isArray` errors propagate, including `TypeError` for revoked proxies.

name: ensureSet
summary: Returns an existing Set unchanged, creates a Set from array items, or treats another supplied value as one member.
description: Use this for inputs that accept one item, an array or a Set. Strings remain whole. Use [toSet](#tosetvalue) to extract other supported collection contents into a new Set.
tooltip: Without arguments, creates a fresh empty Set; explicit `null` and `undefined` remain members. Preserves Sets without consuming their members. Array input follows native Set iteration and equality; other values remain single members. A preserved Set is not a copy.
notes:
Existing Sets retain their identity, including empty, frozen, subclassed and foreign Sets. Own properties and iterator overrides are not read when preserving a Set. Changes through a mutable result also affect the original Set. `Object.freeze` does not prevent adding or removing Set members.

Arrays produce a new local Set using native array iteration. Duplicate values are removed using native Set equality; nested arrays and objects remain references. Sparse array slots normally supply `undefined`. Custom array iterators are honoured and may run application code or throw. Other inputs, including strings, Maps, typed arrays, generators, functions and promises, are stored as single members without iteration, coercion or awaiting.

Omitting the argument creates a fresh empty Set. Explicit `null` and `undefined` create one member. Additional callback arguments are ignored. Native construction and iterator-closing errors propagate unchanged.

Requires native `Set`. Captured native receiver checks recognise existing Sets without consuming their members. If none remain, opaque non-array object inputs throw rather than risk nesting an existing Set. Empty construction, primitive members and array input remain usable where native construction permits them. Missing `Set.prototype.add` prevents construction from supplied members, but preserving a recognised Set and creating an empty Set remain available. See the [runtime guide](runtime.md#optional-capabilities) for the supported receiver checks.

TypeScript infers declared Set and array members, preserves `ReadonlySet` restrictions, and does not promise custom subtype properties. Broad `object` and `unknown` inputs remain conservative. Structural types cannot prove native Set or array identity; treat uncertain imitations as `unknown`. Direct `map(ensureSet)` calls infer broad results; use `map(value => ensureSet(value))` for precise inference.
summaryReturn: The original Set, or a new Set containing array items or one supplied member. With no arguments, a new empty Set.
errors: Missing native Set support throws TypeError before input inspection. Opaque object inputs throw when all captured native identity checks are unavailable. Native construction, revoked-proxy and array-iterator errors propagate; native iteration closes when adding a member fails.

name: isArrayOf
summary: Checks whether a value is an array whose items match a type-name string or predicate.
notes: A type-name string uses native `typeof`: `"object"` includes `null`, and `"number"` excludes Number wrappers. Pass `isNumber` to include Number wrappers. Functions are always predicates; for instance checks, use `value => value instanceof Account`. Length is read once. Empty slots use ordinary indexed reads, including inherited values; a missing value is `undefined`. Matching stops at the first failure.
summaryReturn: `true` if the value is an array and every element matches the matcher, including an empty array; otherwise `false`.
description: Accepts a native `typeof` name or a predicate whose result is evaluated using JavaScript truthiness. Valid empty collections pass without calling predicates. Invalid or missing matchers throw before the input is inspected.
tooltip: Matchers are required and validated before inspecting the collection. Predicates receive one value with no supplied receiver and have their results evaluated using JavaScript truthiness. Empty collections pass without calling predicates. Returned promises are truthy and are not awaited. The check itself returns a primitive boolean.
errors: `TypeError` for invalid or missing matchers. Callback, property-access and native iteration errors propagate.

name: isArrayLike
summary: Checks whether a non-function value has a valid numeric length.
notes: The `length` must already be a primitive number in the accepted range; boxed lengths, negative values, fractions, `NaN` and infinities are rejected. Missing indices are allowed. Reading `length` can invoke a getter or proxy trap.
summaryReturn: `true` if the value is not a function and has a numeric integer length from `0` through `Number.MAX_SAFE_INTEGER`; otherwise `false`.
description: Accepts lengths that are integers from `0` through `Number.MAX_SAFE_INTEGER`. It does not require an iterator or stored values at every index. The length is read once; getters and proxy traps may run.
tooltip: Reads `length` once. Missing indices are allowed; boxed, negative, fractional or non-finite lengths are rejected.
errors: Property getters or proxy traps may throw; their errors propagate.

name: isArrayLikeOf
summary: Checks whether an array-like value contains only items matching a type-name string or predicate.
notes: A type-name string uses native `typeof`: `"object"` includes `null`, and `"number"` excludes Number wrappers. Pass `isNumber` to include Number wrappers. Functions are always predicates; for instance checks, use `value => value instanceof Account`. Length is read once. Empty slots use ordinary indexed reads, including inherited values; a missing value is `undefined`. Matching stops at the first failure.
summaryReturn: `true` if the value is array-like and every indexed value matches the matcher, including an empty input; otherwise `false`.
description: Accepts a native `typeof` name or a predicate whose result is evaluated using JavaScript truthiness. Valid empty collections pass without calling predicates. Invalid or missing matchers throw before the input is inspected.
tooltip: Matchers are required and validated before inspecting the collection. Predicates receive one value with no supplied receiver and have their results evaluated using JavaScript truthiness. Empty collections pass without calling predicates. Returned promises are truthy and are not awaited. The check itself returns a primitive boolean.
errors: `TypeError` for invalid or missing matchers. Callback, property-access and native iteration errors propagate.

name: isPair
summary: Checks whether a value is an array of length two.
summaryReturn: `true` if the value is an array of length `2`; otherwise `false`.
description: Checks the array’s length rather than whether both positions contain values. Sparse arrays of length two pass; array-like objects do not. See [`toMap`](#tomapvalue) and [`toPlainObject`](#toplainobjectvalue) for stricter entry requirements.
errors: Property getters or proxy traps may throw; their errors propagate. Native `Array.isArray` also throws `TypeError` for a revoked proxy.

name: isMap
summary: Checks whether a value is a `Map`.
notes: Uses native collection identity across realms without enumerating or changing the contents. A custom `Symbol.toStringTag` is ignored. A proxy or an object merely inheriting the collection prototype returns `false`. Returns `false` when the local native detection capability is unavailable.
summaryReturn: `true` if the value is a `Map`; otherwise `false`.
description: Recognises native `Map` instances, including from another realm. It does not enumerate or modify the collection. Proxies, prototype imitations and matching tags do not establish native identity.
tooltip: Supports foreign instances without enumerating contents; rejects proxies and prototype or tag imitations. Returns `false` when the local native detection capability is unavailable.

name: isSet
summary: Checks whether a value is a `Set`.
notes: Uses native collection identity across realms without enumerating or changing the contents. A custom `Symbol.toStringTag` is ignored. A proxy or an object merely inheriting the collection prototype returns `false`. Returns `false` when the local native detection capability is unavailable.
summaryReturn: `true` if the value is a `Set`; otherwise `false`.
description: Recognises native `Set` instances, including from another realm. It does not enumerate or modify the collection. Proxies, prototype imitations and matching tags do not establish native identity.
tooltip: Supports foreign instances without enumerating contents; rejects proxies and prototype or tag imitations. Returns `false` when the local native detection capability is unavailable.

name: isWeakMap
summary: Checks whether a value is a `WeakMap`.
notes: Uses native collection identity across realms without enumerating or changing the contents. A custom `Symbol.toStringTag` is ignored. A proxy or an object merely inheriting the collection prototype returns `false`. Returns `false` when the local native detection capability is unavailable.
summaryReturn: `true` if the value is a `WeakMap`; otherwise `false`.
description: Recognises native `WeakMap` instances, including from another realm. It does not enumerate or modify the collection. Proxies, prototype imitations and matching tags do not establish native identity.
tooltip: Supports foreign instances without enumerating contents; rejects proxies and prototype or tag imitations. Returns `false` when the local native detection capability is unavailable.

name: isWeakSet
summary: Checks whether a value is a `WeakSet`.
notes: Uses native collection identity across realms without enumerating or changing the contents. A custom `Symbol.toStringTag` is ignored. A proxy or an object merely inheriting the collection prototype returns `false`. Returns `false` when the local native detection capability is unavailable.
summaryReturn: `true` if the value is a `WeakSet`; otherwise `false`.
description: Recognises native `WeakSet` instances, including from another realm. It does not enumerate or modify the collection. Proxies, prototype imitations and matching tags do not establish native identity.
tooltip: Supports foreign instances without enumerating contents; rejects proxies and prototype or tag imitations. Returns `false` when the local native detection capability is unavailable.

name: isFunction
summary: Checks whether JavaScript reports a value as a function.
notes: Classes, generators and callable proxies pass the native `typeof` check. A class still requires `new`, and a proxy or function can throw when called.
summaryReturn: `true` if `typeof value` is `"function"`; otherwise `false`.
description: Uses `typeof value === "function"`, which includes ordinary functions, classes, generators and callable proxies. Passing does not mean the value can be invoked without `new` or without throwing.
tooltip: Includes classes and callable proxies; does not guarantee a successful call.

name: isDate
summary: Checks whether a value is a `Date`, valid or invalid.
notes: Uses a captured native Date operation across realms. Overridden instance `getTime` methods are ignored. The existence of a Date object and the validity of its timestamp are separate checks.
summaryReturn: `true` if the value is a `Date`, valid or invalid; otherwise `false`.
description: Recognises native Date objects, including from another realm, without relying on their exposed `getTime` method. Use `isValidDate` when a usable timestamp is required.

name: isValidDate
summary: Checks whether a value is a `Date` with a finite timestamp.
notes: Reads the timestamp through a captured native Date operation, ignoring overridden instance `getTime` methods. Dates from another realm are supported; non-Date values return `false`.
summaryReturn: `true` if the value is a `Date` with a finite timestamp; otherwise `false`.
description: Use this after constructing or converting a date when invalid dates must be rejected. Non-Date inputs return `false`; native Date objects from another realm are supported.

name: isInvalidDate
summary: Checks whether a value is a `Date` with a `NaN` timestamp.
notes: Reads the timestamp through a captured native Date operation, ignoring overridden instance `getTime` methods. Dates from another realm are supported; non-Date values return `false`.
summaryReturn: `true` if the value is a `Date` with a `NaN` timestamp; otherwise `false`.
description: Detects an invalid Date object, such as `new Date("not a date")`. It does not classify non-Date values as invalid dates; those return `false`.

name: isRegExp
summary: Checks whether a value is a `RegExp` object.
notes: The browser fallback reads the native regular-expression source getter without executing the expression. Objects from another realm are supported; `RegExp.prototype`, proxies and prototype or tag imitations are rejected.
summaryReturn: `true` if the value is a `RegExp` object; otherwise `false`.
description: Recognises `RegExp` instances, including from another realm, without executing the expression or changing `lastIndex`. Prototype or tag imitations do not pass.

name: isPromise
summary: Checks whether a value passes the local native `Promise` instance check.
notes: The local `Promise` constructor is checked at call time. A promise from another realm can fail, and an object inheriting `Promise.prototype` can pass. The check neither subscribes to a promise nor creates a derived promise. It returns `boolean` in TypeScript.
summaryReturn: `true` if the value passes the local native `Promise` instance check; otherwise `false`.
description: Use this for `instanceof Promise` behaviour in the current realm. A promise from another realm can return `false`, while an object inheriting `Promise.prototype` can return `true`. The check does not call `then` or subscribe to the promise.
tooltip: Uses local `instanceof` semantics; it is not proof of native Promise identity. Does not call `then`.
errors: Native `instanceof` errors propagate, including errors from proxy prototype access or a custom `Symbol.hasInstance` method.

name: isPromiseLike
summary: Checks whether a value is an object or function with a callable `then` method.
notes: Inherited methods, objects from another realm and null-prototype objects can pass. The `then` property is read once; getters or proxy traps may run and throw. The return type is `boolean`: a callable method alone cannot establish TypeScript’s full `PromiseLike<T>` contract.
summaryReturn: `true` if the value is a non-null object or function with a callable `then` method; otherwise `false`.
description: Recognises promise-like values without requiring a native Promise instance, `catch` or `finally`. It does not invoke `then` or verify promise behaviour.
tooltip: Reads `then` without invoking it or checking `catch` or `finally`. Does not verify promise behaviour; getters and proxy traps may run.
errors: Property getters or proxy traps may throw; their errors propagate.

name: isError
summary: Checks whether a value is recognised as an error by the available native check or fallback.
notes: When `Error.isError` is unavailable, the fallback refuses an own or inherited `Symbol.toStringTag` without reading its getter. If the tag key is also unavailable, it returns `false` without inspecting the object rather than trusting a possibly customised tag. Error objects can therefore fail when detection capabilities are missing. When available, the captured native check determines the result. Proxy traps can still run when the fallback has a usable tag key; the result is not a security guarantee.
summaryReturn: `true` if the captured native error check, or its conservative fallback, recognises the value as an error; otherwise `false`.
description: Uses the captured `Error.isError` function when the host provides it. Otherwise, it recognises ordinary untagged Error objects conservatively and rejects custom tags without reading the tag getter. The fallback returns `false` if `Symbol.toStringTag` is unavailable, including for errors.
tooltip: The fallback rejects custom tags without reading their getters. Without native branding or a usable tag key, returns `false`. Proxy traps may run; this is not a security check.
errors: Property getters or proxy traps may throw; their errors propagate.

name: isNode
summary: Checks whether a value is an instance of the local DOM `Node` constructor.
notes: Positive examples require a browser with the corresponding DOM constructor. The constructor is checked at call time; absence produces `false`. Native local-instance rules apply, so this does not validate an object’s properties or recognise every DOM object from another realm.
summaryReturn: `true` if a local `Node` constructor is available and the value passes its instance check; otherwise `false`.
description: Use this for DOM objects from the current browser realm. Returns `false` when the constructor is unavailable; objects from an iframe or another realm may fail the local instance check.
tooltip: Returns `false` when the local constructor is unavailable. Does not recognise all foreign-realm DOM objects.
errors: Native `instanceof` errors propagate, including errors from proxy prototype access or a custom `Symbol.hasInstance` method.

name: isElement
summary: Checks whether a value is an instance of the local DOM `Element` constructor.
notes: Positive examples require a browser with the corresponding DOM constructor. The constructor is checked at call time; absence produces `false`. Native local-instance rules apply, so this does not validate an object’s properties or recognise every DOM object from another realm.
summaryReturn: `true` if a local `Element` constructor is available and the value passes its instance check; otherwise `false`.
description: Use this for DOM objects from the current browser realm. Returns `false` when the constructor is unavailable; objects from an iframe or another realm may fail the local instance check.
tooltip: Returns `false` when the local constructor is unavailable. Does not recognise all foreign-realm DOM objects.
errors: Native `instanceof` errors propagate, including errors from proxy prototype access or a custom `Symbol.hasInstance` method.

name: isDocumentFragment
summary: Checks whether a value is an instance of the local DOM `DocumentFragment` constructor.
notes: Positive examples require a browser with the corresponding DOM constructor. The constructor is checked at call time; absence produces `false`. Native local-instance rules apply, so this does not validate an object’s properties or recognise every DOM object from another realm.
summaryReturn: `true` if a local `DocumentFragment` constructor is available and the value passes its instance check; otherwise `false`.
description: Use this for DOM objects from the current browser realm. Returns `false` when the constructor is unavailable; objects from an iframe or another realm may fail the local instance check.
tooltip: Returns `false` when the local constructor is unavailable. Does not recognise all foreign-realm DOM objects.
errors: Native `instanceof` errors propagate, including errors from proxy prototype access or a custom `Symbol.hasInstance` method.

name: isArrayBuffer
summary: Checks whether a value is a `ArrayBuffer`.
notes: Custom tags are ignored. A detached ArrayBuffer retains its native identity; use the intended buffer operation to determine whether memory is usable. Returns `false` when the local native detection capability is unavailable.
summaryReturn: `true` if the value is a `ArrayBuffer`; otherwise `false`.
description: Recognises native ArrayBuffer objects, including from another realm. Proxies and prototype or tag imitations do not pass. A detached buffer still passes: this check does not establish that its memory can be used.
tooltip: Checks identity rather than memory usability; supports foreign instances and rejects proxies. Returns `false` when the local native detection capability is unavailable.

name: isSharedArrayBuffer
summary: Checks whether a value is a `SharedArrayBuffer`.
notes: Custom tags are ignored. This identifies a shared buffer; it does not validate the memory access or synchronisation required by the caller. Returns `false` when the local native detection capability is unavailable.
summaryReturn: `true` if native shared buffers are available and the value is a `SharedArrayBuffer`; otherwise `false`.
description: Recognises native shared buffers, including from another realm, without accepting proxies or prototype or tag imitations. Returns `false` when the host does not provide `SharedArrayBuffer`.
tooltip: Supports foreign instances and rejects proxies or prototype imitations. Returns `false` when native shared buffers are unavailable. Returns `false` when the local native detection capability is unavailable.

name: isArrayBufferView
summary: Checks whether a value is a native typed array or `DataView`.
notes: Native view identity survives detachment. Proxies and objects that merely inherit a view prototype are rejected. A passing result does not guarantee that a later memory operation will succeed. Falls back to native DataView and typed-array identity checks when `ArrayBuffer.isView` is unavailable; returns `false` if none of those checks is available.
summaryReturn: `true` if the value is a native typed array or `DataView`; otherwise `false`.
description: Uses native `ArrayBuffer.isView` to recognise views, including detached views and views from another realm. Ordinary arrays, proxies and prototype imitations return `false`.
tooltip: Detached views retain their identity; passing does not guarantee usable memory. Falls back to native DataView and typed-array identity checks when `ArrayBuffer.isView` is unavailable; returns `false` if none of those checks is available.

name: isTypedArray
summary: Checks whether a value is a native typed array, including a Node.js `Buffer`.
notes:
Includes subclasses, foreign instances, Node.js Buffers and detached or out-of-bounds views. Uses native view identity and the built-in typed-array tag getter rather than an exposed custom tag.

The declaration describes the common typed-array surface; it does not identify the element type or guarantee usable memory. Uses captured native tag or length getters; returns `false` if no usable native detection getter is available. Missing `Symbol`, `Reflect` or `ArrayBuffer.isView` does not prevent loading.
summaryReturn: `true` if the value is a native typed array, including a Node.js `Buffer`; otherwise `false`.
description: Accepts number and bigint typed arrays, subclasses and foreign instances. Ordinary arrays and `DataView` objects are excluded. Detached or out-of-bounds views still pass because this checks identity, not memory usability.
tooltip: Excludes `DataView` and ordinary arrays; detached views still pass. Does not identify a particular element type. Uses captured native tag or length getters; returns `false` if no usable native detection getter is available. Missing `Symbol`, `Reflect` or `ArrayBuffer.isView` does not prevent loading.

name: isDataView
summary: Checks whether a value is a `DataView`.
notes: Custom tags are ignored; proxies and prototype imitations return `false`. Detached and out-of-bounds views retain their identity, so a passing result does not guarantee that a later memory operation will succeed. Returns `false` when the local native detection capability is unavailable.
summaryReturn: `true` if the value is a `DataView`; otherwise `false`.
description: Recognises native `DataView` identity, including from another realm, without accepting proxies or prototype/tag imitations. Identity does not guarantee usable memory: detached or out-of-bounds objects retain their identity.
tooltip: Checks identity rather than memory usability; supports foreign instances and rejects proxies. Returns `false` when the local native detection capability is unavailable.

name: isAsyncIterable
summary: Checks whether a value exposes an asynchronous iterator method.
notes:
Checks the explicit `Symbol.asyncIterator` protocol. A synchronous iterable does not pass solely because `for await...of` could adapt it. A callable method need not return a valid iterator.

When `Symbol.asyncIterator` is unavailable, the result is `false` and the input is not inspected. Returns `false` without inspecting the input when `Symbol` itself or `Symbol.asyncIterator` is unavailable.
summaryReturn: `true` if the async-iterator symbol is available and the value has a callable `Symbol.asyncIterator` method; otherwise `false`.
description: Returns `true` when `Symbol.asyncIterator` is available and callable on the value. It does not invoke the method, and a synchronous-only iterable does not pass just because `for await...of` could adapt it.
tooltip: Does not invoke the method. Returns `false` without inspecting the value when `Symbol.asyncIterator` is unavailable. Returns `false` without inspecting the input when `Symbol` itself or `Symbol.asyncIterator` is unavailable.
errors: Property getters or proxy traps may throw; their errors propagate.

name: isIteratorLike
summary: Checks whether a value is an object or function with a callable `next` method.
notes: Reads `next` without calling it. This cannot distinguish synchronous from asynchronous iteration or guarantee a valid `IteratorResult` object.
summaryReturn: `true` if the value is a non-null object or function with a callable `next` method; otherwise `false`.
description: Detects the shape of an iterator without advancing it. The method may be synchronous or asynchronous; this check does not validate the values returned by `next`.
tooltip: Does not invoke `next` or validate iterator results. Property getters and proxy traps may run.
errors: Property getters or proxy traps may throw; their errors propagate.

name: isNotNullish
summary: Checks whether a value is neither `null` nor `undefined`.
notes: The generic declaration narrows to `NonNullable<T>`. Values such as `0`, `false`, `""`, `NaN` and `0n` are retained.
summaryReturn: `true` if the value is neither `null` nor `undefined`; otherwise `false`.
description: Use this check to retain present values, including `0`, `false` and the empty string. It can be passed to `Array.filter` and narrows the TypeScript result to `NonNullable<T>`.

name: isJson
summary: Checks whether primitive or boxed string text is valid JSON.
notes: Uses the captured `JSON.parse` function and ignores boxed-string conversion overrides. JSON scalar text passes as well as object or array text. Parse errors produce `false`; no parsed value is retained for the caller. Syntax validity does not enforce unique object keys, finite numeric results or lossless numeric parsing.
summaryReturn: `true` if the value is primitive or boxed string text that parses as JSON; otherwise `false`.
description: Accepts text representing JSON objects, arrays or scalar values such as `"42"` and `"null"`. It does not return the parsed value, check a schema, or test whether an arbitrary object can be serialised. Use `parseJson` when you need the parsed result.
tooltip: Accepts text representing JSON objects, arrays or scalar values. Does not validate a schema or arbitrary-object serialisability.

name: isSetOf
summary: Checks whether a value is a native Set whose items match a type-name string or predicate.
notes: A type-name string uses native `typeof`: `"object"` includes `null`, and `"number"` excludes Number wrappers. Pass `isNumber` to include Number wrappers. Functions are always predicates; for instance checks, use `value => value instanceof Account`. Uses captured native iteration and ignores overridden instance iterators. Iteration is live; predicates must not mutate the collection. Matching stops at the first failure.
summaryReturn: `true` if the value is a `Set` whose items all match the matcher, including an empty `Set`; otherwise `false`.
description: Accepts a native `typeof` name or a predicate whose result is evaluated using JavaScript truthiness. Valid empty collections pass without calling predicates. Invalid or missing matchers throw before the input is inspected.
tooltip: Matchers are required and validated before inspecting the collection. Predicates receive one value with no supplied receiver and have their results evaluated using JavaScript truthiness. Empty collections pass without calling predicates. Unavailable native constructors return `false`; a detected collection without the required native iteration operation throws `TypeError`. Returned promises are truthy and are not awaited. The check itself returns a primitive boolean.
errors: `TypeError` for invalid or missing matchers. Callback, property-access and native iteration errors propagate.

name: isMapOf
summary: Checks whether a value is a native Map whose keys and values match their type-name strings or predicates.
notes: A type-name string uses native `typeof`: `"object"` includes `null`, and `"number"` excludes Number wrappers. Pass `isNumber` to include Number wrappers. Functions are always predicates; for instance checks, use `value => value instanceof Account`. Uses captured native iteration and ignores overridden instance iterators. Iteration is live; predicates must not mutate the collection. Matching stops at the first failure. Both matchers are validated in key/value order before inspection; each key is checked before its associated value.
summaryReturn: `true` if the value is a `Map` whose keys and values match their respective matchers, including an empty `Map`; otherwise `false`.
description: Accepts a native `typeof` name or a predicate whose result is evaluated using JavaScript truthiness. Valid empty collections pass without calling predicates. Invalid or missing matchers throw before the input is inspected.
tooltip: Matchers are required and validated before inspecting the collection. Predicates receive one value with no supplied receiver and have their results evaluated using JavaScript truthiness. Empty collections pass without calling predicates. Unavailable native constructors return `false`; a detected collection without the required native iteration operation throws `TypeError`. Returned promises are truthy and are not awaited. The check itself returns a primitive boolean.
errors: `TypeError` for invalid or missing matchers. Callback, property-access and native iteration errors propagate.

name: toArray
summary: Converts a synchronous iterable, plain object or supported array-like input to a new shallow array.
notes:
Functions, boxed primitives, Dates and RegExps are rejected before inspecting iterator or length properties. Other non-string primitives are unsupported. On eligible inputs a synchronous iterator takes precedence over object properties and indexed values. The iterator method is read once and called with the original input as receiver; null or undefined permits fallback, while other non-callable methods throw.

Plain objects include null-prototype and foreign-realm objects. Own string and symbol keys are snapshotted in property order; each current enumerable descriptor is checked and each included value is read once. Inherited and non-enumerable properties are excluded, newly added keys are not copied, and deleted or newly hidden keys are skipped. A length property is ordinary property data.

Only non-plain array-like inputs use indexed fallback. Their length must be a primitive number that is an integer between zero and Number.MAX_SAFE_INTEGER, matching isArrayLike; strings, fractions and coercible objects are rejected. Length is read once and indexed values are read live. Missing slots become explicit undefined and inherited numeric values are included. Strings iterate by Unicode code point. Nested values retain identity.

Ordinary promises and native async-only collections without a supported synchronous source are rejected. No input is awaited. A plain async-only object is copied as data, including an enumerable async-iterator symbol and its value. Finite one-shot iterators are consumed; infinite iterables do not finish and very large inputs can exhaust memory. Requires native Array.from. Object copying requires Reflect.ownKeys or Object.getOwnPropertySymbols; if both are missing it throws instead of silently discarding possible symbol keys.

If a copied object has an enumerable nullish Symbol.iterator value, the value captured during source dispatch is reused; its getter is not read a second time. Other selected property values are read live after checking their current descriptor.
summaryReturn: A new shallow array containing iterable items, plain object property values or indexed array-like values.
description: Consumes synchronous iterables first, copies plain object property values second, and reads supported non-plain array-like inputs third. Plain object copying includes own enumerable string and symbol properties, including a property named length. Nullish input and unsupported values throw instead of producing an empty array.
tooltip: Consumes iterable input, copies values from own enumerable string and symbol properties, or reads supported array-like indices. Array-like lengths must already be numeric safe integers at least zero. Nullish and unsupported inputs throw. Requires native `Array.from`; missing support throws `TypeError` before inspecting the input.
errors: TypeError for nullish or unsupported input, malformed iterators or invalid array-like lengths. Oversized array results can throw RangeError. Getter, proxy and iterator errors propagate. Missing native Array.from throws before conversion; object copying requires symbol-enumeration support.

name: toBigInt
summary: Converts a value to a primitive bigint using native conversion.
notes:
Empty and whitespace-only strings become `0n`. Fractional or non-finite numbers throw `RangeError`; invalid integer text throws `SyntaxError`; `null`, `undefined` and symbols throw `TypeError`. Number inputs may already have lost precision before conversion.

Native BigInt support requires Node.js 10.4 or later. Without it, this operation throws `TypeError` before coercing the input. Importing the package and using other functions still works.
summaryReturn: The converted primitive bigint.
description: Accepts booleans, integral numbers and integer text, including hexadecimal, binary and octal forms. Use bigint or integer text when exactness matters: conversion cannot recover precision already lost in a Number. Native BigInt support is required only when this conversion is called.
tooltip: Requires native BigInt. Fractional numbers and invalid integer text throw; input conversion hooks may run.
errors: `RangeError` for fractional or non-finite numbers; `SyntaxError` for invalid integer text; `TypeError` for nullish values, symbols, or unavailable native BigInt support. Object-coercion errors propagate.

name: toBoolean
summary: Converts a value to a boolean using JavaScript truthiness.
notes:
Non-empty strings such as `"false"` and `"0"`, arrays and boxed `false` values are truthy. Objects are not unboxed and their conversion hooks are not called. The browser object `document.all` retains its platform-defined falsy behaviour.

For deliberate text parsing, use a separate parser such as go-booleans parseBool. Boolean parsing is not part of this helper and go-types does not add a runtime dependency on that package.
summaryReturn: `true` if the input is truthy under JavaScript boolean coercion; otherwise `false`.
description: Returns the input’s JavaScript truthiness. It does not parse text: `"false"`, `"0"`, arrays and boxed `false` values are truthy. Object conversion hooks are not called.
tooltip: Uses truthiness rather than parsing boolean text. Does not invoke object conversion hooks.

name: toDate
summary: Converts a value to a `Date`, returning existing `Date` objects unchanged. The result can be invalid.
notes:
Date objects from any realm, subclasses and invalid Dates are returned unchanged. For other inputs, `new Date(value)` treats numbers as millisecond timestamps and strings as date text. Invalid text can produce an invalid Date; symbols, bigints and failed coercions can throw. Omitted or `undefined` input produces an invalid Date rather than the current time.

Prefer ISO date-time strings with an explicit timezone for portable string input. Standard date-only strings use UTC, while date-time strings without a timezone use local time; non-ISO parsing is runtime-dependent. Validate with `isValidDate` when needed. The TypeScript result is `Date`, not the input subtype: a structurally compatible input can require a new Date that lacks the input’s extra properties.

examples.expression: (() => { const date = new Date(0); return toDate(date) === date; })()

summaryReturn: The original `Date`, or a new `Date` constructed from the input; it may be invalid.
description: Date objects retain their identity, including invalid dates and dates from another realm. Other inputs use `new Date(value)`. Invalid text and omitted input can produce an invalid Date; use `isValidDate` when a valid timestamp is required.
tooltip: Preserves existing Date objects. May return an invalid Date; omitted input does not mean the current time. Symbols, bigints and conversion hooks can throw.
errors: Symbols, bigints and failed object coercion can throw. Invalid date text can instead produce an invalid `Date`; check with [`isValidDate`](#isvaliddatevalue).

name: toInteger
summary: Converts a value to a number and truncates it towards zero.
notes:
Converts the whole value, so `"12px"` becomes `NaN` rather than `12`. Negative fractions truncate towards zero, unlike `Math.floor`. `NaN`, infinities and signed zero follow `Math.trunc` behaviour.

Number rounding, overflow and underflow happen before truncation. The operation does not clamp values or substitute defaults. Use `isInteger` or `isSafeInteger` to validate the result. Symbols and failing object conversions can throw.
summaryReturn: The numeric conversion truncated towards zero; it may be `NaN` or infinite.
description: Uses `Number` followed by `Math.trunc`, so `"12px"` becomes `NaN` rather than `12`. Negative fractions move towards zero. The result can still be `NaN`, infinite or outside the safe-integer range.
tooltip: Does not guarantee a finite or safe integer. Symbols and failing conversion hooks can throw.
errors: Symbols and failed object conversions can throw. `NaN` and infinity are returned rather than rejected.

name: toJson
summary: Serialises a value to JSON text using native `JSON.stringify` behaviour.
description: Produces JSON text from objects, arrays and scalar values. Strings are encoded as JSON strings, even when they already contain JSON text. Accepts a native replacer callback or property-name list and optional indentation.
summaryReturn: JSON text, or `undefined` when native serialisation produces no text, including omitted input without a replacer.
tooltip: May return `undefined`. Does not transform Maps, Sets or bigints automatically. Cycles and unhandled bigints throw; getters, `toJSON` methods and replacer callbacks can run.
notes:
Without a replacer, top-level `undefined`, functions and symbols produce `undefined`; corresponding object properties are omitted and array positions become `null`. Non-finite numbers become `null`. Native `toJSON` methods apply, including Date serialisation. Ordinary Maps and Sets produce `{}` unless their own properties or custom hooks provide content.

A replacer callback receives `(key, value)` with the containing object as `this`, including a root call with key `""`. It runs after `toJSON` and may replace the root, omit properties or handle bigints. A replacer array selects string/number property names, including at nested object levels; duplicates are ignored. Other replacer-array elements are ignored except boxed strings/numbers, which native serialisation accepts. The `space` argument controls indentation, capped at ten spaces or ten string code units; non-whitespace indentation can produce text that is not valid JSON.

Native errors propagate unchanged. Shared references are allowed; circular traversal throws. Hooks may mutate input or throw, and no input or hook result is awaited. No cycle marker, Map/Set encoding, bigint representation or global polyfill is introduced. Exact escaping follows the host JSON implementation; output is not an HTML-safe escaping or canonicalisation service.
errors: Cycles and unhandled bigints throw `TypeError`. Getter, proxy, `toJSON` and replacer exceptions propagate unchanged.

examples.expression: toJson({a: 1, secret: 2}, (key, value) => key === 'secret' ? undefined : value)

name: toMap
summary: Converts a plain object or iterable of key/value pairs to a new Map.
summaryReturn: A new Map containing a plain object's own enumerable properties as entries, or the supplied key/value pairs. Omitted or nullish input produces an empty Map.
description: Copies own enumerable string and symbol properties of plain objects, or consumes synchronous iterables of exact two-element array pairs. Synchronous iteration takes precedence on eligible inputs. Keys may have any type and are never coerced. Omitted, null or undefined input creates an empty Map.
tooltip: Plain object entries come from own enumerable properties with string or symbol keys. Iterable pairs must be exact two-element arrays with both own indices present. Duplicate keys keep their first position and take the last value. Nullish input creates an empty Map. Requires native `Map`; missing support throws before inspecting the input.
errors: TypeError for unsupported input, malformed iterators or entry pairs that are not exact two-element arrays with both own indices. Getter, proxy and iterator errors propagate. Entry validation errors close the outer iterator. Missing native Map throws before conversion; object copying requires symbol-enumeration support.
notes:
Functions, boxed primitives, Dates and RegExps are rejected before iterator inspection. Plain objects include null-prototype and foreign-realm objects. Own string and symbol keys are captured once in property order; each current descriptor is checked before its enumerable value is read once. Inherited and non-enumerable properties are excluded, deleted or newly hidden keys are skipped, newly added keys are excluded, and nested values retain identity. Numeric property names become string keys; symbol keys stay symbols. An own constructor or length field is ordinary data.

A synchronous iterator takes precedence over object properties on eligible inputs. Its method is read once and called with the original input as receiver. A null or undefined iterator permits object conversion; other non-callable methods throw. Async iterators are never invoked or awaited. A plain async-only object is copied as a record, including enumerable symbol properties. Ordinary promises and native async-only collections without a supported synchronous source are rejected.

Each iterable entry must be an actual array of length exactly two, with own properties at both indices 0 and 1. Explicit undefined keys and values are valid. Holes, inherited-only indices, extra elements, strings and array-like entry objects are rejected. Any key type is allowed, without string coercion. Non-empty strings yield primitive entries and throw; an empty string yields no entries. There is no array-like source fallback.

Native SameValueZero key equality merges repeated NaN keys and treats negative and positive zero as the same key. The last value for a repeated key wins without moving its insertion position. Entry validation and property-access errors inside the loop close the outer iterator; the original error wins over a cleanup error. Native for-of failures while reading next, done or value propagate without an additional close attempt.

Finite one-shot iterators are consumed once; infinite inputs do not finish and no work limit is imposed. Requires native Map. Object copying requires Reflect.ownKeys or Object.getOwnPropertySymbols; missing both throws instead of dropping possible symbol keys.

If a copied object has an enumerable nullish Symbol.iterator value, the value captured during source dispatch is reused; its getter is not read a second time. Other selected property values are read live after checking their current descriptor.

name: toNumber
summary: Converts a value to a primitive number using JavaScript’s `Number` conversion.
notes:
Native conversion accepts whitespace, unlike `isNumeric`. It does not parse locale-specific formats or enforce a safe numeric range. Decimal text and bigints can round to the nearest representable number. Large magnitudes can overflow to infinity and tiny magnitudes can underflow to zero; no exact-decimal or safe-integer guarantee is made.

Symbols throw `TypeError`. Object conversion hooks may run and throw. Omitting the argument passes `undefined` to native conversion and produces `NaN`, unlike a zero-argument call to `Number()`.
summaryReturn: The converted primitive number; it may be `NaN` or infinite.
description: Converts the entire input: `null`, `false` and blank strings become `0`; `true` becomes `1`; `undefined` and invalid numeric text become `NaN`. Text and bigints may lose precision; large magnitudes may overflow and tiny magnitudes may underflow to zero. This does not parse locale-specific numbers or guarantee a finite or safe result.
tooltip: May return `NaN` or infinity, lose bigint precision, round numeric text, underflow to zero, or invoke object conversion hooks. Symbols throw.
errors: Symbols throw `TypeError`. Object-coercion errors propagate; invalid numeric text returns `NaN`.

name: toPlainObject
summary: Creates a plain object from key/value pairs, or makes a shallow copy of an existing plain object.
notes:
Strings, other primitives, boxed primitives, functions, Dates, RegExps and non-iterable class instances are unsupported. Use `parseJson` to parse JSON text and `isPlainObject` to check the parsed result when an object is required.

A synchronous iterator takes precedence over copying object properties. Each entry must be an actual two-element array with both own slots present; an explicit undefined value is allowed. Extra or missing elements, strings and array-like entry objects are rejected. Duplicate keys use the last value. Keys are primitive strings or symbols and are never coerced. Special names such as __proto__, constructor, prototype and toString become ordinary own data properties.

Object copying snapshots own keys, checks each current enumerable descriptor and reads each included value once. Inherited and non-enumerable properties are omitted. Getters may mutate the source or throw. Results have writable, enumerable, configurable data properties and preserve nested references. TypeScript makes inferred properties optional because enumerability and presence cannot be proved structurally. Prototype-name properties and broad string-keyed objects also have unknown values because an omitted own key can expose an inherited property.

Consumes a synchronous iterable once; infinite inputs do not finish. Entry validation or property access in the loop closes the outer iterator, running return/finally cleanup. The original conversion error takes precedence over a cleanup error. Native for-of protocol failures in next, done or value propagate without an additional close attempt. Async iteration is never consumed or awaited. Async generators are unsupported; a plain async-only object is copied as a record, including enumerable symbol properties. Symbol enumeration requires Reflect.ownKeys or Object.getOwnPropertySymbols when copying records; missing both throws rather than silently discarding symbol keys. Array-entry conversion remains available.

If a copied object has an enumerable nullish Symbol.iterator value, the value captured during source dispatch is reused; its getter is not read a second time. Other selected property values are read live after checking their current descriptor.
summaryReturn: A fresh ordinary object containing the copied enumerable properties or supplied entries.
description: Shallow-copies a plain object or consumes synchronous entry pairs. Every result has the local Object.prototype. Strings, nullish input and other unsupported values throw TypeError.
tooltip: Returns a fresh ordinary object. Copies own enumerable string and symbol properties, preserving nested references. Entry pairs must be two-element arrays with string or symbol keys. Strings and nullish input throw.
errors: Unsupported inputs, malformed entry pairs and unsupported keys throw TypeError. Getter, proxy and iterator errors propagate without replacement.

name: toSet
summary: Converts a synchronous iterable, plain object or supported array-like input to a new shallow Set.
summaryReturn: A new Set of iterable items, plain object property values or indexed array-like values, or an empty Set for omitted or nullish input.
description: Uses the same source order as toArray: synchronous iterable values, then values from a plain object's own enumerable string and symbol properties, then supported non-plain array-like indices. Native Set equality removes duplicates while preserving first-insertion order. Omitted, null or undefined input creates an empty Set.
tooltip: Copies iterable values, values from own enumerable string and symbol properties, or supported array-like indices. Lengths must be numeric safe integers at least zero. Nullish input creates an empty Set; unsupported inputs throw. Requires native `Set`, independently of `Array.from`; missing support throws before inspecting the input.
errors: TypeError for unsupported input, malformed iterators or invalid array-like lengths. Getter, proxy and iterator errors propagate. Missing native Set throws before conversion; object copying requires symbol-enumeration support.
notes:
Functions, boxed primitives, Dates and RegExps are rejected before inspecting iterator or length properties; non-string primitives other than nullish input are also unsupported. A synchronous iterator takes precedence over object and indexed data. Its method is read once and called with the original input as receiver; null or undefined permits fallback, while other non-callable methods throw.

Plain objects include null-prototype and foreign-realm objects. Own string and symbol keys are snapshotted in property order, current enumerability is checked, and each included value is read once. Inherited and non-enumerable properties are excluded. A length property is copied as ordinary data. Object copying requires Reflect.ownKeys or Object.getOwnPropertySymbols; missing both throws instead of omitting possible symbol keys.

Only non-plain array-like inputs use indexed fallback. Length must be a primitive number that is an integer between zero and Number.MAX_SAFE_INTEGER, matching isArrayLike. Length is read once and values are read live; missing slots yield undefined and inherited indices can supply values. Strings yield Unicode code points and Maps yield entry arrays. Values retain their identities.

Native SameValueZero equality merges repeated NaN values and treats negative and positive zero as the same value. Distinct objects remain distinct; repeated references collapse. The result is a fresh local Set.

Ordinary promises and native async-only collections without a supported synchronous source are rejected. Plain async-only objects are copied as data, including enumerable symbol values, without invoking their async iterator. No input is awaited. Iterators are consumed once; infinite iterables do not finish and no work limit is imposed. Requires native Set but does not require Array.from.

If a copied object has an enumerable nullish Symbol.iterator value, the value captured during source dispatch is reused; its getter is not read a second time. Other selected property values are read live after checking their current descriptor.

name: toString
notes:
`null` becomes `"null"` and `undefined` becomes `"undefined"`, not an empty string. Primitive symbols use their descriptive string. Arrays and objects use native string conversion, which may call object hooks.

Boxed symbols do not use the primitive-symbol path and throw under native conversion. Objects that cannot produce a primitive also throw.
summaryReturn: The converted primitive string; nullish inputs become their literal text.
description: Uses ordinary string conversion rather than JSON serialisation. `null` becomes `"null"`, `undefined` becomes `"undefined"`, and primitive symbols use their descriptive text. Arrays and objects follow their native conversion rules.
tooltip: May invoke conversion hooks and throw, including for boxed symbols. Does not perform JSON serialisation.
errors: Native conversion errors propagate, including boxed symbols and objects that cannot produce a primitive.
summary: Converts a value to a primitive string using JavaScript’s `String` conversion.

name: toSymbol
summary: Converts a value to a primitive symbol, preserving existing symbols and unboxing `Symbol` wrappers.
notes:
Symbol wrappers, including those from another realm, are unboxed without calling overridden conversion hooks. Other inputs use `Symbol(description)`, which may execute description-conversion hooks and throw.

Each description creates a fresh symbol; `Symbol.for` is never called implicitly. An existing registry symbol keeps its identity when passed in. Omitted or `undefined` input creates a symbol without a description. Requires native `Symbol`; missing support does not prevent loading. Requested conversion throws `TypeError` before inspecting the input when it is unavailable.

examples.expression: (() => { const symbol = Symbol('key'); return toSymbol(Object(symbol)) === symbol; })()

summaryReturn: The original or unboxed symbol, or a new symbol created from the description.
description: Primitive symbols retain identity, and wrappers are unboxed without invoking their overridden conversion hooks. Other inputs use `Symbol(description)`: repeated descriptions create distinct symbols, and no global registry is used.
tooltip: Preserves primitive symbol identity and unboxes wrappers. Other inputs create a new symbol and may invoke description-conversion hooks. Requires native `Symbol`; missing support does not prevent loading. Requested conversion throws `TypeError` before inspecting the input when it is unavailable.
errors: Native description-conversion errors propagate. Unavailable native `Symbol` support throws `TypeError` before conversion.

name: box
description: Creates native wrappers for primitive values without invoking conversion hooks. Existing objects, functions, `null` and `undefined` retain their identity; this is a shallow operation.
summaryReturn: A native wrapper for a non-nullish primitive; otherwise the original object, function or nullish input.
summary: Wraps non-nullish primitives in their native wrapper objects, preserving objects and nullish values.
tooltip: Does not call conversion hooks. Existing objects and functions, `null` and `undefined` are returned unchanged.
notes: No input coercion hooks are called. Uses captured native `Object` boxing. Strings, numbers, booleans, symbols and bigints become wrappers. Omitted input returns `undefined`. Held symbol and bigint primitives can still be boxed when their public constructors are unavailable. No recursive transformation is performed.

name: unbox
description: Reads the stored primitive value of native wrappers without calling overridden conversion hooks. Other values retain their identity; missing native `Symbol`/`BigInt` unboxing support leaves those wrappers unchanged.
summaryReturn: The wrapper’s primitive value when its native unboxing operation is available; otherwise the original input.
summary: Extracts the primitive value from a wrapper object, leaving other values unchanged.
tooltip: Uses captured native `valueOf` intrinsics without calling custom conversion hooks. Missing `Symbol` or `BigInt` unboxing support leaves those wrappers unchanged.
notes: No input coercion hooks are called. Supports `Boolean`, `Number`, `String`, `Symbol` and `BigInt` wrappers from any realm, including subclasses.
