Does not call arbitrary `valueOf`, `toString` or `Symbol.toPrimitive` methods, read custom tags, or traverse proxies. Dates, ordinary objects, functions, prototype imitations and proxies around wrappers are returned unchanged. Omitted input remains `undefined`. If a corresponding native unboxing intrinsic was unavailable during module initialisation, that wrapper remains unchanged. TypeScript retains the original object type and all possible primitive payload types: structural properties cannot prove a wrapper brand, even when an object is typed as `Number` or has custom properties.

name: toRegExp
description: Uses native pattern syntax without escaping text or parsing slash-delimited strings as regex literals. Local RegExp objects can retain identity when `flags` are omitted or `undefined`; copied expressions start with `lastIndex` zero.
summaryReturn: A `RegExp`, which may retain input identity under native rules.
summary: Converts a pattern and optional flags to a `RegExp`.
tooltip: Uses native `RegExp` syntax and `flags`. May reuse a local `RegExp` object without explicit `flags`; copied expressions start with `lastIndex` zero.
notes: Uses native `RegExp` function-call semantics for `RegExp` objects and construction for other input. A local `RegExp` object with its ordinary constructor and omitted or `undefined` `flags` retains identity and `lastIndex`. Foreign expressions, subclasses with their ordinary constructors, and inputs with explicit `flags` produce a new expression. Regex-shaped ordinary objects never receive the native identity shortcut. Native `Symbol.match`, `source`, `flags` and coercion rules still apply, including observable getters. Pattern text is not escaped, and slash-delimited text is not parsed as a JavaScript regex literal. Omitted or `undefined` input creates an empty expression. Supported syntax and `flags` depend on the host; this function does not execute or bound the cost of matching.
errors: Invalid patterns or `flags` throw `SyntaxError`. Native coercion, getters and proxy errors propagate unchanged.

name: toPromise
description: Uses captured native `Promise.resolve` semantics to adopt a promise or thenable, or fulfil with another value. Functions remain values; they are not callbacks to invoke.
summaryReturn: A native `Promise` that adopts the input; ordinary local promises retain identity.
summary: Converts a value to a native `Promise`, adopting thenables and preserving ordinary local promises.
tooltip: Preserves ordinary local `Promise` identity, assimilates thenables and wraps other values. Requires native `Promise.resolve`; functions are values, not callbacks.
notes: Omitted input fulfils with `undefined`. Foreign promises and thenables are adopted with native resolution timing and receiver rules. Then getter or method errors become rejections; native `Promise` constructor lookup can throw synchronously. Rejections are not swallowed. Functions are not called, callbacks are not promisified, and errors thrown while evaluating arguments occur before conversion. TypeScript returns `Promise<Awaited<T>>`. If `Promise` or its resolve operation was unavailable at module initialisation, requested conversion throws before reading the input. No polyfill is installed.
errors: Missing `Promise.resolve` support throws `TypeError` before input inspection. Native synchronous errors propagate; native resolution failures produce rejected promises.

examples.expression: (() => { const value = Promise.resolve(3); return toPromise(value) === value; })()

name: parseJson
summary: Parses JSON text into a JavaScript value using native `JSON.parse` behaviour.
description: Parses JSON text representing objects, arrays or scalar values. An optional native reviver can transform or delete parsed values, including replacing the root.
summaryReturn: The parsed value, or any root value returned by the reviver, including `undefined`. TypeScript returns unknown until the caller validates it.
tooltip: Uses captured native `JSON.parse`, including input coercion, reviver order and errors. Parsing does not validate an application schema; reviver results are not awaited.
notes:
Native input coercion happens once before parsing; non-string inputs such as numbers, booleans and `null` follow `JSON.parse` rules. Omitted or `undefined` input and invalid JSON throw `SyntaxError`; symbol input throws `TypeError`. Nested strings that contain JSON text remain strings. Duplicate object names use the last value, and JSON numbers follow native `Number` precision and range.

A reviver is called for children before parents, then for the root with key "". Its this value is the containing object. Returning `undefined` deletes an object property, leaves an array hole or replaces the root with `undefined`. Other return values are retained as-is, including promises. Non-callable revivers are ignored by the native parser. Newer hosts may pass `source` context as a third argument; older supported runtimes do not. Both the context and its `source` property are optional in the declarations.

Native parsing creates own data properties for names such as `__proto__`; no property-copying or prototype assignment is added. Revivers may deliberately mutate their holder, return arbitrary objects or throw. JSON input coercion and reviver errors propagate unchanged. No automatic `Date`/`Map`/`Set` revival, JSON5 parsing, fallback value or generic type assertion is introduced.
errors: Invalid JSON, omitted input and `undefined` throw `SyntaxError`. Symbols throw `TypeError`. Input coercion and reviver errors propagate unchanged.

examples.expression: parseJson('1', (key, value) => typeof value === 'number' ? value + 1 : value)
